title: Setting up the Talos Arctica electron microscope and Gatan K2 direct detector for high-resolution cryogenic single-particle data acquisition
protocol: Navigate to an empty square and change to a magnification within the SA lens series.
In Digital Micrograph, go to Camera → Prepare Gain Reference.
Follow prompts.
Collect new hardware dark references every day of data collection.
Move to an intact square on the calibration grid and determine eucentric height \(Z-shift).
With the objective aperture removed, determine proper focus at a magnification of SA 45000x using Digital Micrograph to display the Fourier Transform of a live image.
Center the C2 aperture \(70 µm) and stigmate the C2 lens.
At proper focus and eucentric height, align the beam tilt pivot points.
At a magnification of 120000x, determine the rotation center alignment of the objective lens.
Change to SA 45000x magnification.
While in diffraction mode, insert the objective aperture \(100 µm).
Move the aperture off-center so that the edge of the aperture is overlapping the gold powder diffraction rings.
Adjust using the focus knob until the edge of the objective aperture is as sharp/crisp as possible.
Using the intensity knob, minimize the width of the gold powder diffraction rings.
Make note of the beam intensity value for image acquisition.
Adjust exposure rate using changes in spot size only.
Repeat steps B.1-7 if aperture or magnification changes.
Center the objective aperture.
Stigmate the objective lens.
Navigate to an empty square at 45000x magnification.
Set binning = 1 and click on “Full CCD” in Digital Micrograph.
Set exposure time of 1 second and start view.
Adjust exposure rate using changes in spot size only if necessary.
Repeat steps B.1-8 if aperture or magnification changes.
Adjust the total movie exposure time to yield a cumulative exposure of ~50-65 e-/Å².
Adjust the per-frame exposure time (e.g., 100-250 ms) to yield a per-frame cumulative exposure greater than 0.8 e-/Å²/frame.
Move to an intact square on the calibration grid and determine eucentric height and proper focus.
Create a preset that uses the same magnification and intensity settings as the exposure preset.
Set this preset to use a defocus of -3e-7 µm.
Acquire 924x924 (binned by 2) images with a 2 second exposure.
Go to the “Beam Tilt Image” node.
Set Tableau Type: beam tilt series-power in the settings.
Set Beam Tilt: 0.005 radians.
Set Number of tilt directions: 4.
Set Start angle: 0.
Set Correlation type: phase.
Set Tableau binning: 2.
Set beam tilt count: 14.
Click on the “Simulate target” icon in the Beam Tilt Image node.
Ensure the opposing images in the resulting tableau have approximately the same amount of astigmatism and Thon ring spacing.
If adjustments are necessary, repeat the rotation center alignment step.
